data.description:
# Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene

## Problem statement

The player ship currently has **no firing capability at all** — the GDD (§2.3) promises auto-fire, but the `Player` entity only renders and moves. This item gives the ship its first real weapon: a default single-shot **cannon** firing in the direction of travel, plus **three weapon power-ups** (Spread, Dual, Rapid) that swap the equipped weapon **persistently** (no timer — active until another weapon power-up is collected), and a **fourth power-up** that returns the ship to the starting cannon. A new `GymWeapons` scene demonstrates spawning, collection, and the shot patterns round-robin.

> **Deviation from GDD:** GDD §4.4 P1/P2 ("Spread Shot", "Rapid Fire") are *timed* (10 s). Per operator, weapon power-ups here are **persistent until replaced** — the GDD's weapon semantics need a documentation update to match (in scope as documentation).

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each weapon's shot pattern in isolation, collect the power-ups, and verify that weapon switching is instant, persistent, and that the Reset power-up returns to the starting cannon.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a reusable weapon catalogue (pattern + fire rate + bullet visuals per weapon), a heading-based fire direction model, and shared power-up spawn/lifecycle timing reusable by the sibling power-up gyms.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to fly over a grown weapon power-up to collect it, so my ship immediately starts firing that weapon's pattern in my direction of travel.
- As a **player**, I want my collected weapon to stay active until I collect a different one, so there are no surprise "power-downs" mid-run.
- As a **player**, I want angled pattern shots (e.g. Spread, or a hypothetical 180° shot) to be relative to my direction of travel, so if I'm travelling right (90°) a backward shot flies at 270°.
- As a **developer**, I want spawn/lifetime/grow/shrink timings shared and parameterised between the weapon gym (7 s) and the non-weapon power-up gym (5 s), so cadence differences are configuration, not duplicated code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Auto-fire weapon system:** The player ship auto-fires its equipped weapon in the direction of movement (current velocity heading; most-recent heading when stationary) with no fire button (GDD §2.3). Four weapon definitions exist — **Cannon** (single bullet), **Spread** (3-bullet fan: -30°/0°/+30° relative to heading), **Dual** (2 parallel bullets offset perpendicular to heading), **Rapid** (single bullets at a markedly higher rate) — each with its own fire rate and distinct bullet appearance, as tunable constants.
- [ ] **AC2 — Persistent switching + reset:** Collecting a weapon power-up instantly equips its weapon. The equipped weapon persists **with no timer** until another weapon power-up is collected. Collecting the **Reset** power-up returns the ship to the starting **Cannon**.
- [ ] **AC3 — GymWeapons scene + round-robin lifecycle:** A new `GymWeapons` scene (auto-discovered by the gym index, key `GymWeapons`, label `Weapons`) renders the ship (thrust movement + screen-wrap, "← INDEX" back button) and spawns the drops **Spread → Dual → Rapid → Reset** round-robin, one at a time, stationary at a fixed position. Each drop is on screen for **7 seconds** (tunable), growing from scale 0 to full size on spawn and shrinking to nothing on despawn (delta-time driven, framerate-independent), and is removed after its lifetime if uncollected.
- [ ] **AC4 — Collection gating:** A drop is collectible once its current scale is **≥ 3% of full size** (during grow, hold, and shrink while above threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop (drop radius + ship hull radius). Collecting a drop plays the pickup cue and applies its weapon effect; collecting does not pause or reset the next spawn's cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Shared timing infrastructure:** The spawn/lifetime/grow/shrink timing used by this scene is implemented in **shared, parameterised code** (extracted during this implementation so it is reusable by the sibling power-up gym AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT): weapon drops use the 7 s lifetime, non-weapon drops use 5 s, via configuration — no duplicated spawn code.
- [ ] **AC6 — Distinctive visuals + audio:** Each power-up is visually distinctive (code-drawn neon, matching the project's no-asset art style) and its shape visually hints at its shot pattern (fan arc for Spread, parallel bars for Dual, waveform for Rapid, return/undo arrow for Reset). Audio cues play on **spawn, despawn, and collection** (Web Audio synthesis via `src/audio/effects.ts`, safe no-op fallback as today).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: pattern direction math (e.g. a 180° backward shot with heading 90° → absolute 270°), heading-from-velocity with most-recent-heading fallback when stationary, per-weapon fire rates, round-robin order, grow/shrink lifecycle, the ≥ 3% collection threshold, persistent (un-timed) switching, and Reset returning to Cannon. Scene tests (gameHarness) verify auto-discovery, ship presence, auto-fire producing bullets, and collection swapping the weapon. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, the GDD (§2.3 auto-fire and §4.4 weapon power-up semantics — persistent vs timed), the gym index scene list, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — no external art assets; bullets are drawn graphics like the existing `ScoutBullet` (no physics bodies).
- **Threat-free gym:** no enemies, no enemy bullets, no collision damage — player bullets are demonstration-only: they fly in their pattern and are removed off-screen. (Combat-coupled demonstration belongs to sibling AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40.)
- **Out of scope (per operator):** the power-up status **HUD** (tracked in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) and non-weapon/non-combat power-up behaviours (P5/P8/P9 in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) and combat-coupled behaviours (P3/P4/P6/P7 in AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40).
- **Dependency floor:** this item **depends on** AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT (dependency edge added) — the shared power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics are expected to exist or be extractable when this is implemented; this item's implementation extracts the shared, parameterised timing library.
- **Firing direction:** from the current velocity vector (atan2); when speed ≈ 0, fire along the **most recent** non-zero heading; angled shots are offsets relative to that heading (a 0° offset fires straight along travel). Default heading before any movement is configurable (e.g. 0° = right).
- **Spawn cadence (assumption):** one drop on screen at a time; the next drop spawns as the previous despawns (7 s cadence, consistent with the sibling 5 s cadence). Tunable.
- **Fire-rate defaults (assumption, tunable constants):** Cannon ≈ 400 ms, Spread ≈ 600 ms, Dual ≈ 500 ms, Rapid ≈ 125 ms; bullet speed ≈ 350 px/s; grow-in ≈ 0.5 s, shrink-out ≈ 0.5 s inside the 7 s lifetime (~6 s at full size).

## Existing state

- `Player` entity (`src/entities/Player.ts`) renders + moves (thrust/flame); **no weapon, firing, or bullet code exists** anywhere in `src/` for the player.
- Movement model (`src/utils/movement.ts`) exposes `vx`/`vy` in the movement state — the heading source. `Player` keeps `_movementState` privately; a heading accessor or velocity getter is needed.
- Bullet precedent: `ScoutBullet` (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) — a Graphics-based bullet with `vx`/`vy`, advanced by the scene and removed off-screen. The formation gym scenes (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) own bullet lifecycles.
- Gym infrastructure: auto-discovery via `import.meta.glob` on `src/scenes/gym/*.ts` (no registry edits needed for a new scene), `addBackToIndexButton` (`src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`), gameHarness tests (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`).
- Audio: `src/audio/effects.ts` has synthetic spawn/destruction cues and a safe no-op fallback; pickup/spawn-despawn/weapon-change cues will be added here.
- Sibling power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (depends-on, currently intake-complete) delivers the generic power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics + standalone HUD; **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** (sibling, combat-coupled) also depends on it.
- GDD §2.3 specifies auto-fire; §4.4 P1 (Spread Shot, 3-bullet fan) and P2 (Rapid Fire) are currently timed (10 s) — reconciled to persistent semantics by this item (documentation update).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable **weapon catalogue + heading math** module (e.g. `src/utils/weapons.ts`): per-weapon definitions (name, pattern offsets, fire rate, bullet colour/shape), `absoluteAngle = heading + offset`, and bullet creation data from a heading.
2. Extend the **Player** entity: expose heading (velocity-derived, most-recent fallback), an equipped-weapon slot with `equipWeapon(id)`/`resetWeapon()`, a fire cooldown, and auto-fire emission suitable for the scene to spawn bullets.
3. Add a **player bullet** (Graphics-drawn, `vx`/`vy`, removed off-screen) + scene-owned bullet lifecycle in the gym scene (patterned on the enemy gym bullets).
4. Add **weapon power-up drops** (Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset): code-drawn distinctive shapes, grown/shrunk by scale, collectible ≥ 3%, applying weapon equip/reset on collection, leveraging the shared spawn mechanics from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT, extracting the shared parameterised timing.
5. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — ship + auto-fire + round-robin spawner (7 s) + collection + back button; auto-discovered by the index.
6. Add audio cues (spawn/despawn/pickup/weapon-change) to `src/audio/effects.ts`.
7. Tests (unit + scene harness) and documentation (GDD, README, code comments).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — NEW — pure weapon catalogue (patterns, rates, bullet visuals) + heading-relative angle math.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — add heading, weapon slot (`equipWeapon`/`resetWeapon`), fire cooldown + auto-fire emission.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — NEW — Graphics bullet (circle) with `vx`/`vy`, off-screen removal.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — NEW — auto-fired ship + round-robin weapon-drop spawner (7 s) + collection + back button.
- `src/powerups/…` / shared timing — reuse/extract shared spawn/lifecycle code from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with parameterised lifetime (7 s here / 5 s there).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add spawn/despawn/pickup/weapon-change cues.
- `src/core/constants.ts` (or a new weapon-config module) — tunable lifetimes, fire rates, grow/shrink windows, scale threshold.

## Risks & assumptions

- **GDD semantics deviation (timed → persistent weapons):** the GDD currently defines P1/P2 as timed (10 s) effects; this item makes weapon power-ups persistent until replaced. Mitigated by the documentation AC (AC8) — a GDD update explicitly reconciling §4.4 weapon semantics.
- **Scope of "implied" work:** the player ship has zero firing code today; the baseline auto-fire + cannon + weapon-switch machinery is the bulk of the work, not the power-ups themselves. Plan accordingly (this is a feature, not a tweak).
- **Sibling dependency (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT):** shared spawn/lifecycle mechanics may not exist yet when implementation starts; the design assumes the shared parameterised timing is extractable from (or contributed back to) the sibling. The dependency edge + explicit extraction AC (AC5) keep this honest — surface a blocker work item if the sibling's shared code is unusable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD, non-combat (P5/P8/P9) and combat-coupled (P3/P4/P6/P7) power-up behaviours are deliberately out of scope and live in sibling items (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT, AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40). Any new power-up/mechanic discovered during implementation should be recorded as a linked work item, not folded into this one.
- **Direction edge cases:** firing when stationary (use most-recent heading), and before any movement (configurable default heading, e.g. 0° = right) — covered by pure heading math + unit tests (AC7).
- **No physics bodies:** bullets and collection use distance/overlap checks on Graphics (project precedent), not Phaser Arcade bodies; keep it that way for consistency.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (this item **depends on**): "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" — generic power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics (5 s cadence) + standalone HUD; source of the shared timing to extract/parameterise.
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** (sibling): "Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups…" — also depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT; shares the extracted spawn library.
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** (completed): "Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" — `GymPlayer` + `Player` foundation.
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)**: §2.3 auto-fire, §4.4 power-ups (P1/P2 timed semantics to be reconciled).
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed): "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD" — §7.3 audio design this implementation follows.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The three additional shot patterns — what should they be? (suggestions: spread/fan, dual side-by-side, rapid-fire burst, or something else?)" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "as you suggest" → **Spread (3-bullet fan), Dual (2 side-by-side), Rapid (burst)**.
- Q2: "Firing mechanism — auto-fire or fire button?" — Answer: **auto-fire** (matches GDD §2.3).
- Q3: "Direction of shots — all patterns fire in direction of travel?" — Answer: **yes, direction of movement (or most recent movement)**; angled shots are relative to that direction — "if a power up fires a shot backwards (180 degrees) and the ship is travelling to the right (90°) the shot will be at 270°".
- Q4: "Visual design for power-ups?" — Answer: operator delegated — **make them very distinctive from one another, each providing a visual clue to its shot pattern** (fan arc, parallel bars, waveform, undo/return arrow).
- Q5: "Audio — collection sound? spawn/despawn cues?" — Answer: **yes and yes**.
- Q6: "Shooting rate — one rate or per-weapon?" — Answer: **each weapon has its own fire rate**.
- Q7: "Relationship to existing power-up gym item AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT?" — Answer: **separate items** — the existing one covers non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9); a third intake (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40) covers combat-coupled ones; this covers weapon power-ups. All three separate but related.
- Q8: "7 s vs 5 s on-screen?" — Answer: **7 s for weapons, 5 s for others** — shared code manages the difference; this item **depends on** AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT and **extracts the shared library** when implementing.
- Q9: "HUD scope?" — Answer: **out of scope** for this item (tracked in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.
